page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, providing 32 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-core capabilities and weaker single-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall into the bottom 25%, while multi-core metrics, such as the Passmark CPU score and stress-ng multi-core performance, consistently rank in the middle 50%. Memory performance shows a similar divergence; while cached and uncached memory bandwidth read/write speeds are average, the Passmark memory score is weak. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing perform poorly, whereas multi-threaded operations like bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang achieve average throughput.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as a compute-focused resource where memory capacity is secondary to core density. Qualitative cost efficiency is defined by its dedicated core allocation, which prevents resource contention but carries a higher cost per gigabyte of RAM compared to memory-optimized alternatives. Given the average performance in database operations, static web serving, and medium-model LLM inference, the ecs.sn1.7xlarge is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as parallel software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations that can leverage its 32 dedicated cores without requiring high per-core memory allocations.
